purpose: Test whether separate calibration of the unchanged queue-inspired model absorbs CPU-period effects and whether optimistic prediction persists on fresh static tests.
execution: Four hosted runner blocks. On each runner execute ten fresh-stack calibrations, all five quotas at both checkout periods in a hash-fixed interleaved order. Other service CPU periods remain 100 ms. Fit the unchanged model independently for each period, using one post-warmup 60-second quantile per quota. Freeze both models, calibration hashes, one common target quota, four cross-predictions and test order. Upload this checkpoint before either test. Execute two fresh-stack static tests at the common target, one per period, with two post-warmup windows. Counterbalance test order across runners. No external background load and no descending adaptation path.
target_selection: Use the smallest executable thousandth-CPU quota at or above the 100-ms model's guarded 500-ms boundary, clipped below by 0.08 CPU. It must be model-permitted and below 0.30 CPU. This uses only that model's calibration, never the short-period model or test outcomes. If no recommendation exists, run the predeclared 0.14-CPU diagnostic target and mark recommendation evidence unavailable; do not replace the runner for this outcome.
model: Reuse prediction_model.fit/predict/permitted unchanged, including parameter grids, log-loss, timeout lower-bound handling and error guard. No CPU-period covariate or empirical correction is added. Fit separate parameters at the two periods to test implicit absorption. No model selection or validation-driven refitting.
measurement: 40 checkout operations/s and 100 advertising requests/s, pinned runtime/workload, fixed VUs and unchanged SLO/error definitions. Checkout+advertising CPU remains 0.70 and the selected eleven-service budget remains 3.4 CPU. RAM is fixed. Create containers without CPU ceilings, wait for health, apply exact integer limits, then start offered-load warmup. Sample all running containers and host CPU/pressure. Restart/OOM remains diagnostic and never overrides SLO labels.
analysis: Independently replay all primary records and refit calibration only to verify the frozen model. Pool both test start cohorts for each session p95, retaining individual windows. Report all four model-period/test-period comparisons: signed error measured-minus-predicted, absolute error and absolute log error for uncensored finite predictions. Main paired diagnostic compares each model with its matching-period test; also report predicted period shift versus observed shift and error of the unchanged 100-ms forecast on both test periods. Report SLO outcomes, delivery, censoring, CPU usage, throttled microseconds per wall second and period-based counters. No frequency threshold or significance claim; four runners are the replication units.
interpretation: Reduced error after changing period without recalibration is not by itself evidence of a generally better model. Matching-period fits test whether coefficients absorb the effect. Success on static endpoints does not validate descending adaptation or explain all earlier errors. This is a distinct campaign: its single calibration window differs from the earlier two-window model validation; results are never pooled.
period_rationale: 20 ms permits all tested quotas, including 0.08 CPU -> 1600 us, above the 1000-us minimum. At 10 ms, 0.08 CPU would require an invalid 800-us quota.
retry: Retry only infrastructure failures with unchanged design, repeating the whole calibration/test runner block. Keep artifacts and select the latest whole attempt, never splice conditions or select a better outcome.
execution_budget: Ten 240-second calibration sessions and two 300-second tests: 50 minutes offered load per runner plus pulls, startup, resets and uploads. Four runners in parallel, 120-minute job cap.
